Test suite audit

26 November 2026 · myharness · static review

Every authored test module has a file-specific risk assessment and an inventory of test-function dispositions. Retain is the default. The proposed removals below are narrowly scoped; conditional consolidations preserve their unique assertions before any deletion.

575files reviewed
4174test functions
5direct removals
1conditional removal
31strengthening findings
11retained review flags

Per file CSV · Full JSON with every test disposition

Scope and verification limits

  • Complete file coverage is a static audit: AST-assisted inventories of test operations/assertions/exception expectations and fixture/parameter distinctions, file-specific risk assessments, and targeted deeper source/helper review. It is not a claim of a literal line-by-line manual read of every source byte.
  • No pytest suite, browser journey, live provider call, external database connection or coverage/mutation run was performed. A direct installer import-checker counterexample was evaluated without starting a watcher or service.
  • Every test is retained except explicit recommendations; no recommendation has been applied. No production functionality or coding guidelines were changed by this audit.
  • Counts are Python test functions, before parameter expansion, not collected/executed pytest cases. Test-named support modules with no test functions remain in the file ledger.
  • The worktree already contained substantial concurrent edits. Three reviewed AL modules moved after the initial inventory; their current reviewed hashes are retained. Recommendations apply to the recorded file hashes.

Proposed removals

tests/test_harness_command.py:85

remove test_redesign_loop_does_not_disturb_the_numbered_steps_or_the_launch_paragraph:85

Both assertions are exact duplicates over the same command text: the 1..15 sequence is already checked by test_original_start_sentence_and_fifteen_steps_are_intact; launch-paragraph uniqueness is checked in _launch_paragraph(), invoked by two retained tests. This standalone test has no distinct setup, input or outcome.

Keep test_original_start_sentence_and_fifteen_steps_are_intact (39) and _launch_paragraph (18), exercised by retained tests at 24 and 91.

Condition: No replacement required; preserve the identified retained coverage/documentation.

tests/test_phase5_acceptance.py:20

remove test_live_exit_and_browser_gaps_are_marked_outstanding:20

Only searches historical acceptance documentation for three phrases and requires a historical outstanding status to remain indefinitely. It cannot establish whether live acceptance is complete, and changing current product behavior cannot make it fail. Preserve the evidence narrative; executable provenance coverage remains in test_demo_phase5 and reporting/browser tests.

Keep historical evidence in docs/v1-acceptance.md and retain tests/test_demo_phase5.py::test_isolated_demo_marks_fixture_provenance_and_live_acceptance_outstanding, which actually runs the controlled workflow.

Condition: No replacement required; preserve the identified retained coverage/documentation.

tests/test_planning_session_cli.py:8

remove test_missing_caller_identity_refuses_without_inventing_session:8

Exactly duplicates the codex/empty environment/None case of test_unavailable_identity_is_never_generated. Production resolve_caller defaults claude_session_id to None, so both invoke the same behavior and expect the same SESSION_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE exception with no additional effect assertion.

Retain test_unavailable_identity_is_never_generated parameter (codex, {}, None), lines 15-23; harness/planning_session_identity.py:19 confirms default None.

Condition: No replacement required; preserve the identified retained coverage/documentation.

tests/test_runtime_recovery.py:757

remove test_successor_initialization_pre_spawn_repeated_planning:757

The entire body imports test_planning_recovery.test_missing_state_prepares_fresh_planning_without_inherited_authority as scenario and calls it with the same registered, monkeypatch, missing and tmp_path fixtures. Both files use the same registered fixture and missing=False/True parameters; both restrict this route to macOS. No distinct setup/assertion/behavior is added.

Keep tests/test_planning_recovery.py::test_missing_state_prepares_fresh_planning_without_inherited_authority[False/True]; delete only this wrapper and its two duplicate parametrized invocations.

Condition: No replacement required; preserve the identified retained coverage/documentation.

tests/test_smoke.py:7

remove test_package_imports_with_version:7

The sole assertion is harness.__version__ == "0.1.0". test_cli_version_flag imports the same package through harness.cli, uses __version__ for --version and already asserts the same exposed value and exit status.

Retain test_cli_version_flag and the remaining startup/error tests. Version consistency with installed package metadata would be a separate meaningful check if desired.

Condition: No replacement required; preserve the identified retained coverage/documentation.

tests/test_sqlite_capabilities.py:46

remove test_report_runtime_facts:46

The only assertion is sqlite3.sqlite_version_info >= (3,0,0); it does not test Harness behavior or an actual required SQLite feature. Its substantive work is test-report metadata, while runtime_prerequisite_context already prints the same diagnostic facts and the FTS5/WAL/advisory tests exercise required capabilities.

Move record_property metadata and any always-visible facts output into the existing prerequisite fixture, then remove this metadata-only test. Retain strict FTS5/WAL/advisory checks unchanged.

Condition: Preserve runtime diagnostic properties/output in the prerequisite fixture first.

Complete finding to issue mapping

Instruction update validation

Independent Architect source review found no actionable problems. Role TOML, unchanged model slots, shared policy parity and whitespace checks passed. The fast verifier executed 2,993 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped; its overall result remains FAIL because of 78 configured timing-budget violations and source movement during execution. Owned-process cleanup completed, and the slow tier was deferred. Raw evidence and issue comments are recorded in the tracking index.

Publication checkout validation

The isolated main-based checkout executed 2,924 passed, 1 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped, with stable source bytes during the run. Overall verification remains FAIL: the existing startup-canary fixture cannot start its copied uv-managed Python on macOS because libpython3.13.dylib is missing. An independent reproduction loads no AL code; see issue #86. No test or production workaround was included. Separately, 70 timing-budget warnings remain; 163 slow files were deferred. This is not a release result. Evidence is recorded in the tracking index.

strengthen al/claude/skills/al/tests/test_docs.py19 functions · mixed

Agent instructions, published schemas and CLI help form shipped operational contracts; phrase checks protect required guidance but some need more semantic assertions. Claude checks shipped Markdown role definitions rather than Codex TOML files; these instructions are consumed by agents and are product contracts.

strengthen test_every_documented_state_command_exists:65

The subprocess return code is not checked and a documented command is searched as an arbitrary substring anywhere in help output. A missing command can pass when its name is embedded in another command or description. The shipped agent-command compatibility contract is valuable.

Require successful help execution, extract the actual argparse subcommand names or probe each documented command with --help, and compare complete command tokens. Keep the instruction/schema contract checks.

Proposed testing standards

These standards were subsequently adopted in repository and AL instructions on 26 November 2026. Test cleanup remains tracked in GitHub.

  1. State the behavior and regression risk each test protects; inspect the production path before changing or deleting it.
  2. Assert observable outputs, state changes and failure outcomes. A symbol, file, key or phrase alone is insufficient unless the existence/shape is itself a meaningful shipped contract.
  3. Preserve security, business rules, edge cases and fixed regressions. Retain uncertain tests and record the concern.
  4. Delete duplicates only after comparing fixtures, parameters, environment/platform guards, helper assertions and all unique checks. Transfer unique assertions before consolidation.
  5. Make invariant loops non-vacuous: require the expected result or scenario before applying all/for assertions.
  6. Use before/after evidence for change claims; compare to a value observed before the mutation, and measure writes on the actual connection or persisted state.
  7. Make tests independent of ordering and unrelated test side effects. Put always-needed diagnostics in fixtures rather than passing metadata-only tests.
  8. Static prompt, schema, packaging, parity and closed-inventory checks can be valuable product contracts; retain those intentionally, while testing runtime consequences where feasible.
  9. Distinguish synthetic/fixture, integration and actual browser/provider evidence. Do not count a disabled parser, source substring or zero exit as proof of unexercised behavior.
  10. During browser execution also inspect layout, overflow, focus, scroll, accessibility and interaction; retain one meaningful full user journey when extracting focused checks.

Supplementary manual and support artifacts

These are outside the active Python test-function count; they were checked for omitted test suites.

  • al/claude/skills/al/tests/test_parity.py.fixture — retain_review. Not matched by pytest Python filename patterns; no repository code reference/materialization rename found. Contains exhaustive cross-host script/reference parity assertions, so do not count as an active Claude test or delete as hollow without clarifying distribution purpose.
  • al/claude/skills/al/tests/test_consistency.py.fixture — retain_review. Not collected; contains Codex-specific role/config/model consistency and forbidden-token guards. No repository import/rename reference found. Record as dormant support artifact, not six additional active test cases.
  • scripts/demo_phase4.py — retain. Meaningful real HTTP client checks against local Postman stand-ins: branch/MR/PR creation and reads, duplicate MR failure, pipelines/workflows/jobs/report/environment/deployment, failed workflow/retry identity/stale staging revision. Not pytest-collected or called by CI; list in manual-check appendix rather than claim execution. No removal candidate.
  • postman/mocks/gitlab/default.js — retain_support. HTTP mock handler for auth-presence, exact encoded project paths, branch/MR creation and duplication, pagination/pipelines/environment/deployment; regex .test calls validate paths and tokens, not test assertions.
  • postman/mocks/gitlab/rate-limited.js — retain_support. Always returns 429 with retry-after=30 to exercise caller recovery; no test assertions or collection nodes.
  • postman/mocks/github/default.js — retain_support. PR/branch/Actions/deployment stand-in with explicit failure/attempt/deployment modes and synthetic auth; no pm.test/pm.expect assertions.
  • postman/gitlab-contract.yaml — retain_support. Declared provider subset consumed by simulation documentation; contains operations and response schemas, no executable assertions.
  • postman/simulations/gitlab-delivery.sim.yaml — retain_support. Routes local GitLab mock; no independent test suite.
  • postman/simulations/github-delivery.sim.yaml — retain_support. Routes local GitHub mock; no independent test suite.
  • al/tests/pytest_locked_fixture.py — retain_support. Constructs offline wheels from actual installed pytest/dependency bytes; tests of generated inner suites are already covered by inventoried outer runtime-profile tests.
